info.title: SemIf decision service
info.description: Serves one conditional answer-slot distribution per request over a chat-completions-shaped route, whose caller must declare the decision schema. The returned probabilities are conditional option scores, not calibrated decision confidence; every response says so in `choices[].semif.probability_status`. A multi-field decision is not supported: one request scores one field, so N fields are N requests (or one `/v1/semif/batch`). Two statuses are router-level rather than per-path and are therefore not repeated under every path: `404 not_found` for a path this server does not answer, and `405 method_not_allowed` for a method it does not answer there. Every route except `GET /health` is gated by `--api-key` when set, and every non-preflight request answers `403 origin_not_allowed` when `--cors-origin` is an exact origin that the request's `Origin` does not match. A preflight `OPTIONS` is answered `204` before both checks, because a browser attaches neither the bearer token nor a CORS decision to it.

get.summary: Liveness and the exact serving configuration
get.description: Never requires the API key, so a supervisor can probe liveness without a secret.

get.summary: The served model, for OpenAI-client compatibility

200.description: The decision. `text/event-stream` when `stream` is true, with exactly one content chunk, one stop chunk, an optional usage chunk, then `data: [DONE]`.

post.summary: Score N independent decisions in one round trip
post.description: An envelope for independent requests, not a multi-field readout: every item runs the same path a standalone request would, and each result carries its own status. The per-decision identity and provenance are per item.

200.description: One result per item, in order. The envelope is always 200; a failed item carries its own status and error body, so one bad item cannot hide the others.

get.summary: Process counters in Prometheus text format

200.description: The OpenAPI description of this service

bearer.description: Required on every route except `/health` when the server was started with `--api-key`.

role.description: `system` and `developer` build the criterion; every other role is evidence.

content.description: A string, or an array of text and `image_url` parts. Any other part type is refused by name. An `image_url` part is refused unless the server was started with --allow-media (it switches to a degraded, server-tokenized readout); media in a `system`/`developer` message is always refused.

url.description: A `data:image/*;base64,...` URI (fingerprinted and size-capped) or, only with --allow-remote-media, an http(s) URL. The string is forwarded to the backend byte for byte.

model.description: Must equal the served model, or the request is 404.

messages.description: The canonical `[system, user]` pair keeps the original prompt byte for byte (`evidence_renderer: system+user`); any other shape folds into a role-labelled transcript (`evidence_renderer: transcript`).

guided_json.description: The vLLM/SGLang native spelling. Must be the object itself; a path or registered name is refused.

logprobs.description: Fills the standard `choices[].logprobs.content` with the per-slot logprobs this readout already computes. The token is the answer-slot letter.

top_logprobs.description: How many ranked slots to include in `top_logprobs`.

stream.description: Answer as Server-Sent Events. The decision is not incremental: the stream carries exactly one content chunk.

stream_options.description: Requires `stream: true`; `include_usage` appends a usage-only chunk before `[DONE]`.

n.description: Only 1: this endpoint scores one distribution, it does not sample.

max_tokens.description: Accepted and echoed in `ignored_parameters`; exactly one position is always returned.

temperature.description: Accepted and echoed in `ignored_parameters`; the readout is deterministic.

DecisionSchema.description: Exactly one field, whose answer set is the option list. Slot order is the schema's enum order: the first value is slot A.

properties.description: One field. Its `enum` or `type` defines the options.

id.description: Deterministic in the prompt hash, so the same decision has the same id.

content.description: The chosen option as JSON, e.g. `{"verdict":false}`.

token.description: The answer-slot letter, which is the token the engine scores.

SemifBlock.description: Everything needed to attribute this decision. `probabilities` and `option_logprobs` are parallel to `values`.

values.description: Schema order: index 0 is slot A.

probabilities.description: Conditional option scores; uncalibrated as decision confidence.

readout.description: Which backend path produced the numbers, in words.

fallback_used.description: True when a slot missed the backend's top-N and /generative_scoring was used. That rate rises with load.

endpoint.description: Index into the configured endpoint list.

input_ids_sha256.description: Text path only: sha256 of `json.dumps(input_ids)`. Null on the media path, where the prompt is server-tokenized.

prompt_sha256.description: Text path only: sha256 of the rendered prompt. Null on the media path.

request_sha256.description: Media path only: sha256 of the request body sent to the backend. Null on the text path.

modality.description: Media numbers must never be pooled with text numbers: the readout and serving_config differ.

server_tokenized.description: Always true: the token ids come from the backend on every path, so no local tokenizer can disagree with the engine that scores. It is therefore not what tells text from media; `modality` is. On the media path the backend's processor expands the image, so the answer-boundary proof does not apply there.

media.description: One provenance object per attached image: kind, mime, decoded bytes, and the sha256 of exactly those bytes (null for a remote URL, whose bytes this server never saw).

serving_config.description: The measured readout configuration. Text: `vllm-openai-logprob-token-ids-v1` (Tier A), `vllm-openai-completions-subset-softmax-v1` (the top-n path), `sglang-native-generate-token-ids-v1`. Media: `vllm-openai-chat-media-token-ids-v1` or `vllm-openai-chat-media-topn-v1`. Text and media numbers must never be pooled, and neither must two different text recipes.

revision.description: The model revision, as given to `--revision`.

evidence_renderer.description: How `messages` were folded into the scored evidence. A given request must produce the same prompt within one value of this key. The `+media` values are a different prompt and must not be compared with the text values.

ignored_parameters.description: Parameters the caller sent that were accepted but had no effect. Never silent.

tokenize_endpoint.description: The backend route this deployment tokenizes through: `POST /tokenize` (vLLM) or `POST /v1/tokenize` (SGLang). There is no local tokenizer, so this is what must answer for any decision to be scored.

prompt_tokens.description: Null on a media request whose backend did not report `usage.prompt_tokens`: the client never saw the tokenized prompt, so it will not invent a count.

status.description: The status this item would have had on its own.

body.description: The item's completion object, or its error object.

media_support.description: What the startup probe proved about scoring an image. `none` means an image request is refused; a refusal message may point a caller here.

media_serving_config.description: The media readout recipe, null when this deployment does not serve media.

tokenizer_matches_served_root.description: Whether the served checkpoint's directory name matches the local `--model` directory. Null when the two could not be compared: no local checkpoint was named, or the backend reported no model root.

tokenize_endpoint.description: The backend route this deployment tokenizes through: `POST /tokenize` (vLLM) or `POST /v1/tokenize` (SGLang). There is no local tokenizer, so this is what must answer for any decision to be scored.

media.description: The media ceilings in force, so both limits are discoverable: the per-image one and the derived request-body one.

param.description: The offending request field, when there is one. The difference between a caller that can fix its request and one that can only read prose.

InvalidRequest.description: The request cannot be answered faithfully. `error.param` names the field.

Unauthorized.description: `--api-key` is set and the bearer token is missing or wrong.

OriginRefused.description: `--cors-origin` is set to an exact origin and this browser origin is not it.

ModelNotFound.description: `model` names something other than the served model.

TooLarge.description: The body exceeds the server's limit.

BackendFailed.description: The backend refused, broke, or answered unusably. Retrying is not obviously wrong, but the cause is not a spent budget.

BackendTimeout.description: The backend used the whole budget without answering, so the caller may reasonably retry.

InternalError.description: This server found itself inconsistent, e.g. a readout whose arity does not match the declared slots. The response body says what disagreed.

ClientGone.description: The request was cancelled while it waited for a worker slot, so no backend readout was spent on it. A `/v1/semif/batch` item carries this status inside the envelope rather than as the response status.
